items.title: Stress-energy tensor, force density and local balance on flat spacetime
items.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set. (a) A \emph{stress-energy tensor} on $\Omega$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge0$ (with $C^0$ meaning continuous), is a $C^k$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field $T$ on $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]: at every $p$, $T(p):V^*\times V^*\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and symmetric, so its inertial components satisfy $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)). (b) Fix the positive numerical constant $c$ and, in each inertial chart, define the component families $\varepsilon_x:=T^{00}$, $\pi_x^i:=T^{0i}/c=T^{i0}/c$ and $S_x^{ij}:=T^{ij}$. These are numerical component and scaling conventions; their transformation is inherited from $T$. No physical units or measurement interpretation form part of this mathematical definition. (c) When $k\ge1$, the \emph{four-force density} of $T$ is the $C^{k-1}$ field with inertial components $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$, where $\partial_a$ are the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. By [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iv) the components $\partial_aT^{ab}$ transform as a vector, so $f$ is a well-defined vector field on $\Omega$, independent of the inertial chart. For $k\ge1$, one says that $T$ is \emph{locally conserved}, or \emph{balanced}, on $\Omega$ when $f=0$ on $\Omega$, and that $T$ is balanced against the four-force density $f$ when $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$. (d) The definition asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field $T$: whether a given $T$ is conserved, whether it arises from an action or a matter model, and whether any of its integrals over a slice converges are separate hypotheses stated elsewhere. No choice principle is used. For a merely continuous tensor ($k=0$), the component conventions and pointwise contractions are defined, while divergence, four-force density and the balance terminology in (c) require the additional $C^1$ hypothesis; no derivative of a merely continuous field is asserted.
items.strategy: Definition of symmetric C^k type-(2,0) fields for k>=0, and of their divergence only for k>=1, with purely numerical component conventions. Symmetry is chart-independent by the rank-two tensor transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]], clause (iii). For k>=1, under an affine inertial transition xprime=Lambda x+a the constant inverse Jacobian in partialprime_a cancels the first Lambda factor in Tprime^{ab}; hence partialprime_a Tprime^{ab}=Lambda^b_d partial_c T^{cd}, clause (iv). This proves chart-independence of the divergence field. The constants and component families in (b) are numerical definitions, not assertions of measured energy or momentum. No conservation, positivity, matter model, slice convergence or choice principle is asserted. The C0 case is well-defined by the existing tensor-field supplier, which permits k=0; the rank-two component law and symmetry use finite linear evaluation and no derivative of T. The observer decomposition expands delta=h-n tensor n pointwise, so its original continuous-T scope and all contraction/uniqueness conclusions are retained. The C1 and higher cases keep exactly the original divergence and balance claims.

items.title: Observer decomposition of a symmetric stress-energy tensor
items.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $\Omega\subseteq A$ open, and let $T$ be a continuous symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c). At a point $p\in\Omega$ define $\varepsilon:=T^{ab}n_an_b$, $\pi^a:=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and $S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Then: (a) $\pi$ lies in $n^\perp$, $S$ is symmetric and horizontal in both slots ($S^{ab}n_b=n_aS^{ab}=0$), and $$T^{ab}=\varepsilon\,n^an^b+c\,(n^a\pi^b+\pi^an^b)+S^{ab}.$$ (b) Contracting with $n$ gives $T^{ab}n_b=-\varepsilon n^a-c\pi^a$; hence $\varepsilon$ and $\pi$ are determined by $T$ and $n$, and the decomposition is unique among decompositions $T^{ab}=\varepsilon' n^an^b+c(n^a\pi'^b+\pi'^an^b)+S'^{ab}$ with $\pi'\in n^\perp$ and $S'$ symmetric horizontal: $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$, $\pi'=\pi$, $S'=S$. (c) In any adapted inertial orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$, the numerical components of this decomposition are $\varepsilon=T^{00}$, $\pi^0=0$, $\pi^i=T^{0i}/c$ and $S^{0a}=S^{a0}=0$, $S^{ij}=T^{ij}$ for $i,j=1,2,3$. Define isotropic rest stress to mean $S^{ab}=p h^{ab}$ for a real scalar $p$, where $h^{ab}:=\eta^{ab}+n^an^b$. Thus $S=0$ means vanishing rest stress, and is the isotropic case $p=0$; isotropy permits any $p$, including nonzero pressure or tension. These are numerical tensor identities. Physical adoption of the energy/momentum-density reading is a separate model premise; this mathematical lemma asserts no observer measurement. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Pointwise linear algebra. Since $h$ is the projection of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\operatorname{span}(n)$, and $\delta^a{}_c=h^a{}_c-n^an_c$, expand $T^{ab}=(h^a{}_c-n^an_c)(h^b{}_d-n^bn_d)T^{cd}$ and use symmetry of $T$ to obtain (a) with the stated signs. For (b), contract (a) with $n_b$ using $n_bn^b=-1$, $n_b\pi^b=0$ and $S^{ab}n_b=0$; uniqueness follows by contracting a general decomposition with $n_an_b$ (gives $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$), with $h_{ac}h_{bd}$ (gives $S'=S$), and with $n_b$ (gives $\pi'=\pi$). No choice principle is used. For (c), in the adapted frame $n^a=\delta^a_0$, $n_a=-\delta_a^0$ and $h^a{}_b=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,1,1)$. Substituting these components into the definitions gives the stated entries. The rest-stress convention $S=p h$ gives $S^{ij}=p\delta^{ij}$ in that frame; it does not force $p=0$. The decomposition needs only continuity of $T$ and its pointwise symmetric tensor structure; no derivative or physical identification is used.

items.title: Compact-support variation: the fundamental lemma, integration by parts and differentiation under the integral sign
items.statement: Work in an inertial chart $x$ of the affine Minkowski model, identifying a nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq A$ with its image in $\mathbb R^4$; all integrals are Riemann (Darboux) integrals. (a) If $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\int_\Omega g\,\psi\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth compactly supported $\psi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, then $g=0$ on $\Omega$. (b) If $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$ and compactly supported and $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$, then for each $a$, $\int_\Omega(\partial_af)g\,d^4x=-\int_\Omega f(\partial_ag)\,d^4x$, provided $g$ is $C^1$ on $\Omega$ and the products are extended by zero outside $\operatorname{supp}f$. (c) Let $s_0>0$. If $F:(-s_0,s_0)\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous with continuous $\partial_sF$ and there is a compact $K\Subset\Omega$ with $F(s,z)=0$ for $z\notin K$ and all $s$, then $s\mapsto\int_\Omega F(s,z)\,d^4z$ is $C^1$ on $(-s_0,s_0)$ with derivative $\int_\Omega\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z$. The lemma is choice-free and is stated for the exact Riemann integration theory on bounded rectangles; no distribution theory, no $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ hypothesis and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
(a) Suppose g(p) is nonzero. Set sigma=+1 if g(p)>0 and sigma=-1 if g(p)<0. By continuity there is a closed nondegenerate box Q compactly inside Omega on which sigma*g>=a>0. Choose a smaller closed nondegenerate box Qprime in int(Q). Apply [[lem-euclidean-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]] to Qprime inside int(Q) to obtain a smooth bump rho with 0<=rho<=1, rho=1 on Qprime and support inside int(Q). Its finite-ball construction gives compact support. Use the signed test psi=sigma*rho. Its integral satisfies integral g*psi=integral (sigma*g)*rho >=a*vol(Qprime)>0, contrary to the hypothesis. Both signs of g(p) are thereby covered.
(b) The products fg, f partial_a g, and g partial_a f have compact support inside Omega. Their extensions by zero are respectively C1 and continuous on R4: near every point outside Omega they vanish on a neighbourhood, because supp(f) is a compact subset of Omega. Choose a bounding rectangle with this support in its interior. On each coordinate line the integral of partial_a(fg) is zero by FTC, since fg vanishes at the endpoints. Apply [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] repeatedly to the continuous functions, and expand the product derivative to obtain the displayed integration-by-parts identity.
(c) Extend F and partial_s F by zero outside Omega. Since the common support K is compactly inside Omega, both extensions are continuous on each compact parameter interval times a bounding rectangle, and differentiation in s gives the extended partial_s F. The imported [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]] has a one-spatial-variable public interface; apply it four times to the iterated coordinate integrals, using Fubini for continuous functions at each stage. Continuity of each integrated derivative follows from uniform continuity on the compact product and the bound |integral u|<=vol(R)*sup|u|. This proves C1 parameter dependence on each compact subinterval of (-s0,s0), hence everywhere there. The compactly supported integral does not depend on its bounding rectangle by [[lem-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-is-well-defined]]. All choices are finite; no AC or countable choice is used.

items.title: First variation of the scalar-field action and the Euler-Lagrange equation
items.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set with an inertial chart $x$, let $c,K>0$ be numerical constants, let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and let $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth real scalar field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]). For every smooth compactly supported $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ define the first variation $$\delta S(\varphi)[h]:=-\frac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh+V'(\varphi)h\Big)\,d^4x,$$ a finite Riemann integral by compact support of $h$ ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c)). Then (a) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=\dfrac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)h\,d^4x$, where $\Box\varphi:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$; (b) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=0$ for every such $h$ if and only if $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$. The equation in (b) is called the scalar-field equation of this model. The statement is the first variation of the action on compactly supported variations; it asserts nothing about convergence of $S$ on unbounded domains, no boundary term, no dynamics beyond the equivalence in (b) and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used. Precisely, with $L(\phi):=\tfrac12\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi\partial_b\phi+V(\phi)$, define the relative action $S_h(s):=-(K/c)\int_\Omega[L(\varphi+sh)-L(\varphi)]\,d^4x$. Its integrand has support in $\operatorname{supp}h$, so it is defined for every real $s$ even when either background action diverges; $S_h\prime(0)=\delta S(\varphi)[h]$.
items.strategy: For a fixed compactly supported h, the density difference L(phi+sh)-L(phi) and its s-derivative are supported in supp(h). On each bounded parameter interval they are continuous with continuous s-derivative, so [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]], clause (c), differentiates the relative action and gives exactly the stated first variation. Apply clause (b) to h and eta^{ab} partial_a phi, noting the metric components are constant, to obtain delta S=(K/c) integral(Box phi-Vprime(phi))*h. Mixed partial symmetry gives the displayed Box formula. If the residual is zero, stationarity follows. Conversely stationarity against every compactly supported h makes the continuous residual vanish by clause (a), including both signs. Neither a full-domain background action nor a boundary condition is used. This is the compact-support flat specialization of Tong (4.42)-(4.43) and its equation-of-motion calculation, with the relative functional made explicit; no choice principle is used.

items.title: The Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action on flat spacetime
items.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be any nonempty open set with inertial chart $x$, let $c,K>0$ be numerical constants, and let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For each smooth symmetric $(0,2)$ tensor $h$ with compact support, set $g_{ab}(s)=\eta_{ab}+s h_{ab}$. Choose $s_0>0$ so that these matrices are nondegenerate with negative determinant for $|s|<s_0$; outside $\operatorname{supp}h$ they equal $\eta$. Put $D_h(s,x):=[\tfrac12 g^{ab}(s,x)\partial_a\varphi(x)\partial_b\varphi(x)+V(\varphi(x))]\sqrt{-\det g(s,x)}$ and define the relative action $$\mathcal A_h(s):=-\frac Kc\int_\Omega[D_h(s,x)-D_h(0,x)]\,d^4x.$$ This is the integral of a compactly supported density difference, without assuming either background density has a finite integral. (a) $\mathcal A_h$ is differentiable at $0$ and $$\mathcal A_h\prime(0)=\frac1{2c}\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x,\qquad T^{ab}:=K[\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_d\varphi\partial^d\varphi+V(\varphi))],$$ with indices raised by $\eta$. (b) $T$ is smooth and symmetric, and is the unique continuous symmetric $(2,0)$ field for which $\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x=2c\mathcal A_h\prime(0)$ for every such $h$. It is called the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of this scalar-field density. (c) The result holds on unrestricted open $\Omega$, uses only compactly supported metric variations, and imposes no convergence or boundary condition at infinity. If the full background action happens to exist, the relative action is its variation difference and gives the same derivative. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
On the compact support of h its entries are bounded. The determinant is a polynomial in s with continuous coefficients, and det(eta)=-1; compactness supplies a uniform s0 for which det(g)<0. The adjugate formula then makes the inverse entries smooth in s and x, as is the square root. Outside supp(h), g=eta. Thus D_h(s)-D_h(0) and its parameter derivative have a common compact support; the compact-variation lemma applies to the relative integral.
Differentiate g^{ac}g_cb=delta^a_b to obtain delta g^{ab}=-eta^{ac}eta^{bd}h_cd=-h^{ab}. Cofactor expansion gives delta det(g)=det(eta)*eta^{ab}h_ab=-eta^{ab}h_ab, so delta sqrt(-det(g))=+(1/2)eta^{ab}h_ab. Therefore delta D=-(1/2)h^{ab}partial_a phi partial_b phi+(1/2)eta^{ab}h_ab L(phi). Multiplication by -K/c gives exactly +(1/(2c))integral T^{ab}h_ab. Symmetry and smoothness follow from the formula. For uniqueness, take a continuous symmetric difference Q: a test with one diagonal component psi gives integral Q^{aa}psi=0; a test with h_ab=h_ba=psi for a<b gives 2 integral Q^{ab}psi=0. The signed fundamental lemma yields every component Q^{ab}=0. Tong (4.46) uses the inverse-metric variation convention; converting it to the covariant variation delta g_ab=h_ab yields the positive sign here. This convention change, compact density difference, and explicit finite-dimensional derivation preserve the source-derived formula without presuming a convergent background action. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Divergence identity for the scalar-field stress-energy tensor
items.statement: In the setting of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]], with $\varphi$ smooth and $T$ the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action, $$\partial_aT^{ab}=K\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)\partial^b\varphi\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$ where $\partial^b=\eta^{bc}\partial_c$ and $\Box\varphi=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$. In particular every solution of the scalar-field equation $\Box\varphi=V\prime(\varphi)$ has conserved tensor, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$. Conversely conservation implies the scalar-field equation at every point where $d\varphi\ne0$, and hence throughout an open set on which $d\varphi$ is nowhere zero. In full generality conservation is equivalent to the pointwise product condition $(\Box\varphi-V\prime(\varphi))d\varphi=0$; it need not imply the scalar equation where $d\varphi=0$. Off shell the balance holds with the four-force density $f^b=K(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial^b\varphi$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Expand $T^{ab}=K(\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_c\varphi\partial^c\varphi+V))$: $\partial_a(\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi)=(\Box\varphi)\partial^b\varphi+\partial^a\varphi\,\partial_a\partial^b\varphi$, and $\partial^b(\tfrac12\partial_c\varphi\partial^c\varphi+V)=\partial^c\varphi\,\partial^b\partial_c\varphi+V'(\varphi)\partial^b\varphi$; the two second-derivative terms cancel after relabeling by symmetry of mixed partials ([[thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem]]) and $\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=\Box$. Source: the direct divergence check is the flat-space restriction of the scalar computation in G6 of the research argument and of the analogous check (4.51) of Tong. No choice principle is used. Write E=Box(phi)-Vprime(phi). The displayed identity is exact off shell. Since K>0 and the metric is nondegenerate, at a point with dphi nonzero at least one raised component partial^b phi is nonzero; zero divergence then forces E=0 there. At points with dphi=0 no such conclusion follows. For example phi=0 and V(s)=s give T=0, divergence zero, and E=-1 on any open Omega. Therefore the unconditional converse is false and is replaced by the exact product criterion and its noncritical-point converse.

items.title: Dust: conservation of rho n tensor n is equivalent to continuity and inertial flow
items.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\rho:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ with $\rho>0$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ field which is future timelike and satisfies $\eta(n,n)=-1$ everywhere (a future unit timelike field, [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)), and set $T^{ab}:=\rho\,n^an^b$ (a $C^1$ symmetric $(2,0)$ field). Then, on $\Omega$, (a) $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ if and only if both $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ (continuity) and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ (inertial flow); (b) if $\rho\ge0$ is allowed to vanish, the implication $\partial_aT^{ab}=0\Rightarrow n^a\partial_an^b=0$ is asserted only on the open set $\{\rho>0\}$, and no assertion is made where $\rho=0$; (c) Under the conservation hypothesis $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ in (a), if $J$ is an interval and $x:J\to\Omega$ is a $C^2$ curve with $x'(s)=n(x(s))$ for all $s$ (an integral curve of $n$), then $x''(s)=0$: the flow lines of an inertial unit field are affine straight lines in the affine structure of $A$. For the nonnegative-density branch in (b), the same conclusion holds for an integral curve whose image lies in $\{\rho>0\}$, under conservation there. The lemma is the exact mathematical content of the dust equations; it asserts no matter model, no interaction and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Expand $\partial_aT^{ab}=(\partial_a\rho)n^an^b+\rho(\partial_an^a)n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$ and rewrite the first two terms as $(\partial_a(\rho n^a))n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$. Contract with $n_b$ and use $n_bn^b=-1$, $n_b\partial_an^b=\tfrac12\partial_a(n_bn^b)=0$ to obtain $n_b\partial_aT^{ab}=-\partial_a(\rho n^a)$. Hence conservation gives continuity, and then the remaining horizontal part gives $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the converse is immediate. For (b), the same contraction gives continuity without dividing by $\rho$; the remaining term is $\rho n^a\partial_an^b=0$, so division is justified exactly where $\rho>0$. For (c), use the conservation antecedent to obtain inertial flow from (a), then differentiate: $x''(s)=n^a\partial_an^b(x(s))=0$ by the chain rule, so $x'$ is constant and $x$ is affine. Source: the equivalence is the flat restriction of the dust computation of G6 and of the dust equations read off from (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong; the positivity hypothesis is stated because the converse needs it. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Perfect fluid: conservation is equivalent to the energy and Euler equations
items.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\varepsilon,P:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) and set $T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$. Write $D\varepsilon:=n^a\partial_a\varepsilon$, $\vartheta:=\partial_an^a$, $a^b:=n^a\partial_an^b$ and $h^{bc}:=\eta^{bc}+n^bn^c$ (these formulas define the first-order expansion scalar, acceleration and raised rest projection for the stipulated $C^1$ field; they agree with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] and [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] when the field is smooth). Then the identity $$\partial_aT^{ab}=n^b\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)+\big((\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP\big)$$ holds on $\Omega$, and consequently $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$ if and only if $D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta=0$ and $(\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP=0$ on $\Omega$. The two equations are the energy-balance and Euler equations of the model; the lemma asserts no equation of state, no thermodynamic relation and no causality condition. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Compute $\partial_aT^{ab}=\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]n^b+(\varepsilon+P)n^a\partial_an^b+\partial^bP$, rewrite $\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]=D\varepsilon+DP+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta$ with $DP=n^a\partial_aP$, and decompose $\partial^bP=h^{bc}\partial_cP-n^bDP$ because $\eta^{bc}=h^{bc}-n^bn^c$; the terms in $DP$ cancel, leaving the displayed identity. The second bracket is horizontal: $n_ba^b=\tfrac12n^a\partial_a(\eta(n,n))=0$ and $n_bh^{bc}=0$. Contracting with $n_b$ gives $-\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)$ and projecting with $h$ gives the second bracket, so the two equations are equivalent to conservation. Source: the flat restriction of the perfect-fluid computation of G6 and of (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong. No choice principle is used. This argument divides by neither $\varepsilon+P$ nor $P$: the degenerate case $\varepsilon+P=0$ is retained. All quantities use at most first coordinate derivatives of the $C^1$ fields.

items.title: Stress balance and finite flux on closed boxes
items.statement: Let $x$ be an inertial chart of the affine Minkowski model with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, let $B:=\prod_{a=0}^{3}[c_a,d_a]$ with $c_a<d_a$ be a closed axis-parallel box, and let $T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on an open neighbourhood of $B$; put $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$ (continuous on $B$) as in [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]. (a) (Box identity.) For each $b$, with $F_a^+:=\{x\in B:x^a=d_a\}$, $F_a^-:=\{x\in B:x^a=c_a\}$ and each face integral the Riemann integral over the remaining three coordinates, $$\int_B f^b\,d^4x=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\Big(\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x\Big).$$ (b) (Slice balance.) Write $K:=\prod_{i=1}^{3}[c_i,d_i]$ and, for $s\in[c_0,d_0]$, $Q^b(s):=\int_K T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$; this is finite and continuous in $s$. For $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K} f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ where $K_i^\pm$ are the two faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. (c) (Finite-flux conservation.) If $f=0$ on $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces $[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^\pm$ for $i=1,2,3$, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for every $b$. The theorem concerns finite axis-parallel boxes in one inertial chart and is proved by the fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a flux identity for arbitrary regions or hypersurfaces, does not assert that $Q^b$ transforms as a four-vector under a change of inertial chart, and asserts no conservation without the stated side-flux hypothesis; no noncompact or limiting statement is made. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: For (a): for fixed values of the remaining coordinates, $x^a\mapsto T^{ab}$ is $C^1$ on $[c_a,d_a]$, so one-variable FTC ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]) gives $\int_{c_a}^{d_a}\partial_aT^{ab}\,dx^a=T^{ab}(d_a)-T^{ab}(c_a)$; integrate this identity over the remaining three coordinates and sum over $a$, using Fubini/iterated integration for continuous functions on rectangles ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[cor-repeated-riemann-integrals-on-rectangles]]) and integrability of continuous functions on boxes ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). For (b): apply (a) to the sub-box $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and identify the first and last faces with $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)$ and the spatial faces with the displayed side-flux terms; continuity of $Q^b$ follows quantitatively: the continuous $\partial_0T^{0b}$ is bounded by some $M$ on the box because continuous rectangle integrability includes boundedness ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]); FTC and the integral bound give $|Q^b(s)-Q^b(r)|\le\operatorname{Vol}(K)M|s-r|$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). (c) is immediate from (b). Source: this is the flat finite-box flux argument of S9 of the research supplier argument, the restricted version of Crowell 9.3.2-9.3.3 pp. 192-195, with the arbitrary-region argument declined. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Hodge reconstruction of an alternating two-tensor and the optional SI field split
items.statement: Let $(V,\eta)$ be the oriented Lorentz vector space of the affine Minkowski model with orientation and volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], and let $F:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be an alternating bilinear form ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]], [[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]]). Define the Hodge dual by $(*F)_{ab}:=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ and set $(\alpha\wedge\beta)_{ab}:=\alpha_a\beta_b-\alpha_b\beta_a$. Use the standard form normalization $F=\tfrac12\sum_{a,b}F_{ab}\theta^a\wedge\theta^b$ in the dual coframe $\theta^a(e_b)=\delta^a_b$ of an oriented orthonormal frame, and define $(F\wedge F)(v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3):=2[F(v_0,v_1)F(v_2,v_3)-F(v_0,v_2)F(v_1,v_3)+F(v_0,v_3)F(v_1,v_2)]$, the alternating four-form exterior square. Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and put $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$. (a) $e(n)=b(n)=0$, and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat:=\eta(n,\cdot)$; also $*(*F)=-F$, so the Hodge dual squares to $-1$ on two-forms. (b) In an oriented orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}$, $b_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$, $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; hence the six components of $F$ are exactly the six components of the pair $(e,b)$ and the reconstruction in (a) is equivalent to these component formulae. (c) The quadratic invariants are $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,(e\cdot b)$, where $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ are those of the spatial structure of the frame ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); also $F\wedge F=2(e\cdot b)\varepsilon$. The two scalar expressions $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ form a basis of the homogeneous quadratic polynomials in the six components of $F$ invariant under the proper orthochronous Lorentz group; the square-wedge expression is dependent, $F\wedge F=-\tfrac12 I_2\varepsilon$. $I_2$ is an oriented pseudoscalar and changes sign if the chosen orientation is reversed with the metric and $F$ held fixed. (d) (Optional SI identification.) Let $c>0$. If in an inertial frame one identifies $F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ for numerical spatial vectors $E,B\in\mathbb R^3$, then $e_i=-E_i/c$ and $b_i=B_i$, the invariants of (c) read $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,(E\cdot B)/c$, and $F\wedge F=-2(E\cdot B)\varepsilon/c$. If $\kappa:=(F\wedge F)(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=(F\wedge F)_{0123}$, then $E\cdot B=-c\kappa/2$. Under the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along $e_1$ with parameter $\beta\in(-1,1)$ one has $E'_1=E_1$, $B'_1=B_1$, $E'_\perp=\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$ where the cross product is the right-handed product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v=\beta c$ along $e_1$. In an SI reading, $c$ has units $\mathrm m/\mathrm s$, $E$ has units $\mathrm V/\mathrm m$ and $B$ has units tesla, so $E/c$ and all components of $F$ have units tesla; these are conditional unit assignments, not measurements. (e) The theorem is algebra on the oriented Lorentz vector space with the stated index and duality conventions; clause (d) is an explicitly optional identification of the components of $F$ with fields the electromagnetic framework names $E,B$, and the theorem asserts no field equation, no dynamics, no measurement and no transformation beyond the stated component law. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: First obtain an oriented rest frame adapted to $n$: the observer decomposition theorem proves $n^\perp$ is a three-dimensional positive inner-product space ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)); apply finite Gram–Schmidt to a basis of it ([[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]) and reverse one spatial basis vector if the resulting frame orientation is negative. This uses only finite choices. Let $a_i=\theta^0\wedge\theta^i$ and $s_1=\theta^2\wedge\theta^3$, $s_2=\theta^3\wedge\theta^1$, $s_3=\theta^1\wedge\theta^2$. The declared dual and volume conventions give $*a_i=-s_i$, $*s_i=a_i$ by direct component evaluation. Thus $*^2=-1$ on all six basis forms, $F=-e_i a_i-b_i s_i$ and $*F=-b_i a_i+e_i s_i$, proving the annihilation, six-component recovery and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$. Raise the time-spatial indices with the diagonal metric and count both orders of each skew pair to get $\frac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4e\cdot b$. The explicitly normalized square wedge has $a_i\wedge s_i=\varepsilon$ and all unmatched terms zero, so $F\wedge F=2e\cdot b\,\varepsilon$; the witness $F_{01}=F_{23}=1$ gives $e_1=b_1=-1$ and square wedge $+2\varepsilon$. The tensor/volume laws ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii),(v)) show that these expressions are invariant under proper Lorentz changes. For completeness of the quadratic invariant claim, spatial half-turns force the three coefficient blocks of a rotation-invariant quadratic polynomial to be diagonal, and proper axis permutations force scalar diagonals; it has the form $A|e|^2+B|b|^2+C e\cdot b$. For $e=(0,1,0),b=0$, an axis-one passive boost gives $e'=(0,\gamma,0),b'=(0,0,\gamma\beta)$; invariance gives $A(\gamma^2-1)+B\gamma^2\beta^2=0$, whence $A+B=0$ for any nonzero allowed $\beta$. Both surviving invariant polynomials are linearly independent by testing $b=0,e\ne0$ and $e=b\ne0$. For the optional SI identification, apply the actual passive boost matrix to the two raised indices of $F$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)). All six entries are $E'_1=E_1$, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-vB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+vB_2)$, $B'_1=B_1$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+vE_3/c^2)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-vE_2/c^2)$, which are exactly the promised vector formulas with the right-handed cross product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Substituting $e=-E/c,b=B$ gives the displayed invariants and standard four-form coefficient $\kappa=-2E\cdot B/c$, hence $E\cdot B=-c\kappa/2$. The zero-boost case gives $\gamma=1$ directly. All arguments are finite-dimensional, choice-free algebra and assert no EM dynamics. The cached Carroll full-text equations (1.79)–(1.88), printed pp.21–23, were read for wedge normalization and the Lorentzian star-square rule; the S8 local research route is independently recomputed, not accepted by citation. Horizontal covectors e,b are identified with their metric-dual vectors in n-perp. Each frame uses its own time-axis observer in the displayed boosted component lists; a fixed observer transforms with the vector law. For P=a|e|^2+b|b|^2+c e dot b, the coefficients are P=-a I1-c I2/4. Optional E,B are pointwise numerical triples; conditional SI units assign E/c and B tesla.

items.title: Adopted continuum matter models and their evolution equations
items.statement:
Adopt, on top of the flat spacetime postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the SI conventions [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and the particle premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], the following classical continuum matter models on an open set $\Omega\subseteq A$ of the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

**(i) Scalar field.** A real smooth dimensionless field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a smooth potential $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with values in inverse square metres ($\mathrm m^{-2}$) and a constant $K>0$ in joule per metre ($\mathrm J/\mathrm m$) have the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ — the Euler–Lagrange equation of the adopted local action density, with stationarity defined by the finite relative action for compactly supported field variations ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]); the model's stress-energy tensor is the Hilbert tensor of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]].

**(ii) Dust.** A $C^1$ rest energy density $\rho:\Omega\to(0,\infty)$ (joule per cubic metre) and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n:\Omega\to V$ ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) satisfy $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the stress-energy tensor is $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$.

**(iii) Perfect fluid.** $C^1$ maps $\varepsilon,P:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ (energy density and pressure), both in joule per cubic metre, and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ satisfy the energy-balance and Euler equations of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; an equation of state or evolution equation determining $P$ is part of the model and is not supplied by this postulate; the stress-energy tensor is $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta^{-1}$, where $\eta^{-1}$ is the symmetric type-$(2,0)$ inverse metric with components $\eta^{ab}$.

**(iv) Additivity.** The total stress-energy tensor of a composite system is the sum of the stress-energy tensors of its constituents (tensor-field addition on $\Omega$).

**(v) Adopted observer readings and units.** For a tensor physically assigned to matter in this model, all inertial components $T^{ab}$ have units joule per cubic metre. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, an ideal observer with future unit direction $n$ and four-velocity $U=cn$ reads the numerical contractions of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] as energy density $\varepsilon_n=T^{ab}n_an_b$, momentum density $\pi_n^a=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and rest stress $S_n^{ab}=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$, where $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$. In an adapted inertial frame these are $T^{00}$, $T^{0i}/c$ and $T^{ij}$ respectively, and the energy-flux components are $cT^{i0}=c^2\pi_n^i$. Momentum density has units kilogram per square metre per second, energy flux has units watt per square metre, and rest stress has units joule per cubic metre. These identifications are adopted model readings, not mathematical facts about an arbitrary symmetric tensor and not reported measurements. If $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ is assigned to external exchange, the spatial components $f^i$ are force per volume and $cf^0$ is power per volume; the corresponding numerical balances are $\partial_t(T^{00})+\partial_i(cT^{i0})=cf^0$ and $\partial_t(T^{0j}/c)+\partial_iT^{ij}=f^j$. Neither assignment selects a force law or asserts conservation.

Scope and status

This postulate adopts model equations and tensor identifications only. It does not assert conservation of the tensors — that is derived from these equations in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]] — does not select any force law, interaction, equation of state, thermodynamic or dissipative behaviour, does not claim that these models exhaust physical matter, and contains no empirical premise, measurement or uncertainty statement. The dimensionless scalar field, the potential with its stated units and the constant $K$ are adopted primitive data of the scalar model; the SI conventions and the identification of the coordinate $x^0$ with $ct$ are those of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], and the observer congruence vocabulary agrees with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] for smooth fields ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).
items.strategy: Adopted physical premise; no proof obligation (the schema records postulates with formulation, scope and sources, not a deduction). The mathematical content used in the formulation is confined to the model equations and the displayed tensors; conservation is deliberately NOT part of this postulate. Sources: the scalar action and equation of motion are 4.5.1 of Tong; the fluid equations are 4.5.4 of Tong and the displayed tensors are (4.53) of Tong, (1.106)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.3-9.2.6 of Crowell; the choice to adopt, rather than derive, the matter dynamics follows the source statements that conservation follows from each model's own equations of motion (Carroll p. 30) and that matter actions and equations of state are separate model assumptions (Tong 4.5). No empirical support is claimed. The observer component reading removed from mathematical definitions/lemmas is explicitly adopted in(v), including the exact c factors: $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ turns the tensor balance into the two displayed SI balances, while the observer-decomposition lemma provides only the numerical contractions/components. This is preservation of the framework's stated interpretation, not a new empirical law or a deduction of an observer measurement. Local relative actions, not a possibly divergent background integral over all Omega, formulate(i).

items.physical_scope: Classical continuum matter in flat affine Minkowski spacetime: a real scalar field with potential, dust and a perfect fluid, with the stated evolution equations adopted as model premises. Excludes gravity, electromagnetic coupling, general relativity, thermodynamics and equations of state, viscosity, dissipation and heat conduction, quantum or statistical matter, and every empirical or measurement claim; the models are adopted, not derived from experiment.

items.title: Adopted total stress-energy and isolation premise for integrated conservation
items.statement:
Adopt as the boundary and isolation premise of the continuum framework the following.

**(i) Total tensor.** In every conservation or integration statement of this framework the tensor used is the total stress-energy tensor of the system considered, including every constituent that carries energy-momentum — matter, fields and supporting structures present in the region — assembled by the additivity clause of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]].

**(ii) Localisation.** Fix an inertial chart with $x^0=ct$. Choose real $s_1<s_2$ and a nondegenerate closed spatial rectangle $\bar K=\prod_{i=1}^3[a_i,b_i]$, $a_i<b_i$. The interval $[s_1,s_2]$ parametrizes $x^0$ in metres; the corresponding coordinate-clock interval is $[s_1/c,s_2/c]$ in seconds. Whenever conservation of a slice four-momentum on this slab is asserted, the model assumes that during that interval the total tensor is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of a closed box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), that its components satisfy the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces of the box for $i=1,2,3$, and that the slice integrals converge; equivalently, the system is isolated inside the chosen region for the chosen interval.

**(iii) Failure of isolation.** If the side flux does not vanish, only the exact finite-flux balance of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] is asserted; no conservation of a slice integral is inferred and no limiting procedure at spatial infinity is adopted.

**(iv) Unmodelled matter.** For a matter system not governed by one of the models of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]], conservation of its stress-energy tensor is not inferred; if used it must be adopted or derived separately.

**(v) Exclusion caution.** Removing a constituent — a support, a field or a container — from the total tensor can make the side-flux condition fail; the premise concerns the total tensor of the system, not an arbitrary partial tensor.

Scope and status

This premise is an idealisation of an isolated bounded system in flat spacetime; it is not a measurement and makes no apparatus, statistical or empirical claim. The localisation clause is a boundary hypothesis on a finite box in a single inertial chart; it neither supplies an equation of motion for the total tensor nor implies the vanishing of the force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$, which is a separate hypothesis of the integration statements that use this postulate.
items.strategy: Adopted physical premise; no proof obligation. The zero-flux condition is exactly the hypothesis of the mathematical finite-flux theorem [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c), so the premise is stated in the form the deduction consumes. Sources: the isolation/vacuum-side argument is 9.3.4 of Crowell pp. 195-197; the flat conserved-charge box argument is 4.5.5 of Tong, including the warning that one must require vanishing current on the timelike boundary; the container/support caution is the reader-recorded defect discussion of Crowell pp. 101-103 and 233-234. No measurement is reported and no empirical claim is made.

items.title: Local conservation of stress-energy for the adopted matter models
items.statement:
Under the matter premises of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]: (a) If $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field solving the adopted field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$, then the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]) satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$, in every inertial chart. (b) If $ho>0$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted dust equations, then $T=ho\,n\otimes n$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely if $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ and $ho>0$ then the dust equations hold. (c) If $\varepsilon,P$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted fluid equations, then $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta^{-1}$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely conservation of that $T$ implies the two fluid equations. (d) For a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted; a conservation statement about such a field is an additional explicit premise. (e) The theorem is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, and its conclusions inherit the scope of the postulate. Under the already stated homogeneous dust reading, the tensor boost computation has the conditional physical interpretation $T'^{00}=\gamma^2ho$. For comoving identical massive particles with fixed rest mass $m$, rest number density $
u$ and $ho=
u mc^2$, a rest rectangular parcel has boosted simultaneous volume $1/\gamma$ times its rest volume (the parallel length contracts and transverse lengths are unchanged), so its particle density is $\gamma
u$; the adopted massive-particle reading gives each particle energy $\gamma mc^2$. Thus the two factors in $\gamma^2ho$ correspond respectively to particle energy and volume/density. This is conditional model interpretation for that homogeneous particle realization, not a derivation of the continuum from microscopic dynamics, a claim about arbitrary tensors, or empirical evidence.
items.strategy: Clause (a) is [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solutions of the adopted field equation; clause (b) is [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]; clause (c) is [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]. Clause (d) records the absence of any derivation for arbitrary prescribed tensors: the local balance $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$ of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] is a definition, and no hypothesis in this page forces $f=0$ for an arbitrary $T$. Clause (e) restates the physical scope. No empirical premise is used and the conclusions inherit only the adopted ideal model readings, with no reported measurement or empirical support. For the preserved dust energy/volume explanation, use the massive-particle energy formula of [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]] and the parallel/transverse length formulas of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] on the stipulated homogeneous rest rectangular parcel. Divide its same particle count by the contracted simultaneous volume and multiply by the particle energy. The exact tensor computation itself is $T'^{00}=\rho(\Lambda^0{}_0)^2=\gamma^2\rho$ from [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]](iii). This physical explanation is restricted to the explicitly interpreted homogeneous dust and introduces no interaction, statistical or measured claim.

items.title: Integrated four-momentum of an isolated system on finite slices
items.statement: Fix $c>0$ and an inertial chart $x$ with $x^0=ct$. Let $\bar K=\prod_{i=1}^3[a_i,b_i]$, $a_i<b_i$, be a nondegenerate closed spatial rectangle and let $s_1<s_2$ be real length-coordinate values, and let $T$ be the total stress-energy tensor of a system in the situation of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]: $T$ is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ there (for the adopted models this is the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other system it is an explicit premise), and satisfies the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces for $i=1,2,3$. Put $Q^b(s):=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ and $P^b:=Q^b/c$. Then: (a) $Q^b(s)$ is finite for every $s\in[s_1,s_2]$ and $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$; (b) consequently $P^b$ is independent of $s\in[s_1,s_2]$; if $P$ is future timelike, its invariant mass $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ is independent of $s$ as well; (c) if the side flux does not vanish, the exact balance is the finite-flux identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]], and no conservation is asserted; (d) no transformation law for $P^b$ under a change of inertial chart or slicing is asserted: without an admissible-region flux argument, $P^b$ is a chart-component integral and is not claimed to be a four-vector; no noncompact, asymptotic or gravitational-energy statement is made, and the reading of $P^b$ as the system's four-momentum is the model's interpretation of the integral, not a measurement.
items.strategy: Clause (a) applies [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c) to the box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ under the stipulated model hypotheses (conservation and vanishing side flux); the invariance of the invariant mass in (b) is immediate because $P$ is a constant future timelike vector and $\eta(P,P)$ is then constant, using the invariant-mass formula of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]. Clause (c) is the general balance case of the same theorem. Clause (d) records the exact scope: the theorem proves constancy of the chart integrals and nothing about their transformation under a change of chart, which would require the oriented hypersurface flux construction; no noncompact limit is taken. No empirical premise is used.

items.title: Scope of the page: two notions of force, conditional conservation and excluded claims
items.statement: The force vocabulary of this framework has two distinct mathematical carriers: the four-force $F=\dot P=dP/d\tau$ on a massive particle worldline ([[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]]; its identities are conditional on [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]) and the four-force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ of the continuum ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Neither is a force law. The page's conservation statements are conditional deductions: local conservation of the scalar, dust and fluid tensors is proved from the adopted model equations ([[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), while for any other matter the conservation of $T$ must be adopted separately. Integrated conservation additionally requires the isolation premise ([[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]) and is asserted only for finite boxes and slices in one inertial chart ([[pthm-sr-integrated-conservation-for-isolated-matter]]). The framework contains no gravity, no electromagnetic coupling, no derivation of an equation of state, no energy conditions (the printed dominant-energy-condition inequality of the Crowell source p. 191 is defective and is not used), no angular-momentum theorem and no empirical premise; no measurement, apparatus or uncertainty claim is made anywhere on this page.
items.strategy: Scope remark; no proof obligation. It records which page claims are adopted premises, which are conditional deductions, and which promised or source-adjacent topics are deliberately not asserted (energy conditions, angular momentum, gravity, electromagnetism, equations of state, asymptotic charges, four-vector transformation of chart integrals). Sources: the errata and scope findings of the Crowell reader report (printed p. 191 defective DEC; pp. 231, 240 field-stress caveats) and the conservation caveats of Tong 4.5.3 and Carroll p. 30 / pp. 138-139.

items.title: Dust stress-energy in a boosted inertial frame
items.statement: In an inertial frame $x$ let dust at rest have constant rest coefficient $\rho>0$, so $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$; the only nonzero component is $T^{00}=\rho$. Consider the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along the $x^1$ axis with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$: $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$. By the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii), $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=0,$$ all remaining components zero; equivalently $T'=\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ where $n'$ is the image of $e_0$ under the boost, $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$, the future unit direction of the dust in the primed frame. The primed coordinate coefficient $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$ is the numerical factorization $\gamma^2\rho=\gamma(\gamma\rho)$. Its source interpretation as one energy factor and one volume factor belongs to the separately adopted dust model reading; it is not an empirical identification proved by this component calculation. All primed components are constant, so $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, consistently with [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. The example is a component computation; it asserts no measurement and no dynamics.
items.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ with the boost matrix $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: only $T^{00}=\rho$ contributes, giving the displayed components; the identification $T'=\rho n'\otimes n'$ follows from $n'=\Lambda e_0$. Constancy and conservation are immediate. Source: Crowell Example 5 p. 185 and (1.106) of Carroll. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Perfect fluid components in its rest frame and in a moving frame
items.statement: Let $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$ be the perfect-fluid tensor of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], with $n$ future unit. In an inertial frame with $n=e_0$ (fluid at rest) the components are $T^{00}=\varepsilon$, $T^{11}=T^{22}=T^{33}=P$ and all other components zero. Let $|\beta|<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$. Under the passive boost along $x^1$ with parameter $\beta$ (so that its primed coordinate velocity is $-\beta c\,e_1\prime$, with speed $|\beta|c$), the component law gives $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P,$$ all remaining components zero. In particular the adapted-frame numerical contraction is $T^{ab}(e_0\prime)_a(e_0\prime)_b=T\prime{}^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P$. Its difference from $\varepsilon$ is $(\gamma^2-1)(\varepsilon+P)$, so equality holds if and only if $\beta=0$ or $\varepsilon+P=0$. It is at least $\varepsilon$ whenever $\varepsilon+P\ge0$; no positivity of $\varepsilon+P$ is assumed here. The transverse diagonal components remain $P$. The computation uses the observer decomposition of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] to identify this numerical contraction; it asserts no equation of state and no measurement.
items.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d[(\varepsilon+P)n^cn^d+P\eta^{cd}]$ using $\eta'=\eta$ (metric preservation, [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]) and $n'=\Lambda n$ with $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$; the displayed components follow. The adapted-frame numerical contraction is clause (c) of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] at $n=e_0'$. Source: (4.53) of Tong, (1.107)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.6 of Crowell. No choice principle is used. Subtracting $\varepsilon$ gives $(\gamma^2-1)(\varepsilon+P)$, and $\gamma^2-1=\beta^2/(1-\beta^2)$ vanishes exactly for $\beta=0$. Thus equality also holds for every boost when $\varepsilon+P=0$, and the inequality has exactly the stated conditional sign.

items.title: A dust solution with constant velocity and transverse density profile
items.statement: Let $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, fix an inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$, let $n:A\to V$ be the constant field with inertial components $n^0=\gamma$, $n^1=\gamma\beta$, $n^2=n^3=0$ (so $\eta(n,n)=-1$), and let $\rho_0:\mathbb R^2\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$ and define $\rho:A\to(0,\infty)$ by $\rho(p)=\rho_0(x^2(p),x^3(p))$. Then $n^a\partial_a\rho=\gamma(\partial_0\rho+\beta\partial_1\rho)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ because $n$ is constant, so $(\rho,n)$ satisfies the dust equations and $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ is conserved by [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. For any nondegenerate finite spatial box $\bar K=[c_1,d_1]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$ whose slab lies in the chart domain, the finite slice integrals $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)d^3x$ are constant in $s$, because $T^{0b}$ is time independent. This also follows from the slice-balance identity [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b): $T^{2b}=T^{3b}=0$, and the two $x^1$-face fluxes $T^{1b}=\rho_0\gamma\beta n^b$ agree pointwise and cancel with opposite orientations. The individual $x^1$-face flux need not vanish. A nonzero transverse profile is not compactly supported in all three spatial variables, since it is independent of $x^1$. The nonnegative variant $\rho_0\ge0$, including compact support in the transverse $(x^2,x^3)$ plane, gives the same exact conserved solution and finite-box constancy, with the zero-density qualification of [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]\,(b). The flow lines are the parallel straight lines $x^1=\beta x^0+\mathrm{const}$, $x^2,x^3$ constant. The example exhibits a family of exact solutions of the dust equations; it asserts no interaction and no measurement.
items.strategy: Verify $\eta(n,n)=-\gamma^2+\gamma^2\beta^2=-1$. Since $n$ is constant, $\partial_an^b=0$ and $\partial_an^a=0$; since $\rho$ depends only on $x^2,x^3$, $n^a\partial_a\rho=0$. Hence both dust equations hold, including for the nonnegative-profile variant, and [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]] gives conservation. On any finite spatial box, $T^{0b}=\gamma\rho_0 n^b$ is continuous and independent of $x^0$, so its finite integral is constant. In the exact slice identity [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b), the divergence term vanishes; the $x^2,x^3$ terms vanish separately and the $x^1$ terms cancel because the integrands and their transverse integration domains are equal on both faces. Clause (c), which requires each side flux to vanish, is not used. The integral curves have constant tangent $n$, hence the stated parallel affine lines. The entire calculation uses prescribed fields and no matter-model or empirical assertion. No choice principle is used.

items.title: A static uniaxial stress: tension must be constant along the stressed direction
items.statement: In an inertial chart let $T^{ab}(x)=\rho(x^1)e_0^ae_0^b+P(x^1)e_1^ae_1^b$ with $\rho,P$ of class $C^1$ on an interval of $x^1$ (a static uniaxial stress field in the $e_1$ direction; $P<0$ is a tension). Then the balance components are $\partial_aT^{a0}=\partial_0\rho(x^1)=0$ and $\partial_aT^{a1}=\partial_1T^{11}=P'(x^1)$, so $T$ is conserved on a connected chart domain if and only if $P$ is constant there; the energy density $\rho(x^1)$ may vary while the tension must be uniform along the stressed direction. This reproduces the static equilibrium condition of a uniform rope under tension and shows that conservation constrains the stress, not the energy density, in this configuration. The example is a component computation and asserts no material model.
items.strategy: The components are $T^{00}=\rho(x^1)$, $T^{11}=P(x^1)$ and all others zero. Thus $\partial_aT^{a0}=\partial_0T^{00}=0$, $\partial_aT^{a1}=\partial_1T^{11}=P\prime(x^1)$, and the $b=2,3$ components vanish. In general the full tensor derivative $\partial_1(\rho e_0\otimes e_0)=\rho\prime e_0\otimes e_0$ is nonzero; it does not enter the divergence because its first tensor index is $0$. Therefore conservation is equivalent to $P\prime=0$ on the interval of $x^1$ values attained in the chart. The $x^1$ range of a connected chart domain is an interval: if an intermediate value $r$ were absent, the nonempty relatively open sets $\Omega\cap\{x^1<r\}$ and $\Omega\cap\{x^1>r\}$ would disconnect the domain. Thus on this interval and [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] makes $P$ constant there. The density profile remains unrestricted apart from its stated $C^1$ regularity. Source: Crowell Example 8 pp. 188-189 with the stated signature conversion; no material model or force law is deduced. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The box balance identity checked on an explicit stress-energy field
items.statement: In an inertial chart define the smooth symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field by $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$, with every other component zero. Its force density is $f^0=2$, $f^1=f^2=f^3=0$. Let $t_1<t_2$, $x_1<x_2$, $c_2<d_2$, $c_3<d_3$, and set $A=(d_2-c_2)(d_3-c_3)>0$, $B=[t_1,t_2]\times[x_1,x_2]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$. For $b=0$, the full four-dimensional identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] reads $\int_B f^0\,d^4x=2A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$. The temporal-face difference is $A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$ and the axis-one-face difference is $A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$; all transverse face terms vanish because $T^{2b}=T^{3b}=0$. For $b=1$, the temporal face integrals $\pm A\int_{x_1}^{x_2}x^1\,dx^1$ cancel, as do the axis-one face integrals $\pm A\int_{t_1}^{t_2}x^0\,dx^0$, so both sides vanish; $b=2,3$ vanish identically. For example, transverse area $A=6$, temporal length $2$ and axis-one length $3$ give bulk integral $72$ and the nonzero face differences $36+36$. This verifies the finite-box identity on a field with nonzero force density and nonzero net side flux; no physical matter model is asserted.
items.strategy: Compute all integrals as three-dimensional face or four-dimensional volume Riemann integrals. Repeated integration of each transverse constant factor gives A, then the FTC computes the remaining integrals. For b=0 the two nonzero face differences add; for b=1 the two opposite-face pairs separately cancel; b=2,3 and all transverse faces vanish. The full finite-box theorem supplies the sign convention and repeated-integration framework. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Null plane-wave scalar field and its conserved stress-energy tensor
items.statement: Let $k\neq0$ be a null covector, $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, with $k^\sharp$ future, let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varphi(x):=f(k_ax^a+\theta_0)$ in an inertial chart; take $V\equiv0$ and $K>0$. Then $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field, $\partial_a\varphi=f'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)k_a$ and $\Box\varphi=k^ak_af''(k_ax^a+\theta_0)=0$, so $\varphi$ solves the massless scalar-field equation of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]. Its Hilbert stress-energy tensor is $$T^{ab}=Kf'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)^2\,k^ak^b,$$ symmetric; wherever $f\prime\ne0$ it is a positive multiple of the rank-one tensor $k^\sharp\otimes k^\sharp$ with future-null generating vector $k^\sharp$, and wherever $f\prime=0$ it is the zero tensor. In either case one has $T^{ab}n_an_b=Kf'^2\,(k_an^a)^2\ge0$ for every future unit observer $n$, and conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, by [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solution $\Box\varphi=0$. In an inertial frame $T^{00}=Kf'^2(k^0)^2\ge0$. The example is an explicit conditional computation for the massless scalar model; it asserts no wave observation and no measurement.
items.strategy: Substitute $\partial_a\varphi=f'k_a$ into the Hilbert tensor formula of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]; the potential term drops and $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$ kills the trace term, leaving $Kf'^2k^ak^b$. The equation of motion holds because $k$ is null, and conservation follows from [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]]. Source: the scalar stress tensor (4.51) of Tong with V=0; the null-covector condition is the framework's own. No choice principle is used. The coefficient $Kf\prime{}^2$ is strictly positive exactly where $f\prime\ne0$ and vanishes exactly where $f\prime=0$, because $K>0$. Since $k^\sharp$ is a fixed nonzero future-null vector, this proves the precise rank-one/zero alternative. Squaring $k_an^a$ gives the nonnegative observer contraction stated without any claim that the zero tensor is future null.

items.title: Divergence-free stress-energy with a nonconserved slice integral
items.statement: In an inertial chart on all of affine Minkowski space define the smooth symmetric field $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=-x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$, with every other component zero. Then $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ everywhere, since the only possibly nonzero divergence components are $\partial_0T^{00}+\partial_1T^{10}=1-1=0$ and $\partial_0T^{01}+\partial_1T^{11}=0$. For $L>0$, $c_2<d_2$, $c_3<d_3$, put $A=(d_2-c_2)(d_3-c_3)>0$ and $K=[0,L]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$. The full spatial slice integral is $Q^0(s)=\int_K T^{00}(s,x)\,d^3x=A Ls$. The axis-one side-flux difference on a slab $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ is $\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_1^+}T^{10}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_1^-}T^{10}\,d^3x=-A L(s_2-s_1)$; all transverse fluxes vanish. Consequently [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] gives $Q^0(s_2)-Q^0(s_1)=A L(s_2-s_1)\ne0$ whenever $s_1<s_2$. For example $A=6,L=2,s_2-s_1=3$ gives $36$. Thus zero local divergence alone does not conserve a finite slice integral: the side-flux/isolation hypothesis of the integrated-conservation theorem cannot be dropped. This prescribed tensor is not claimed to arise from any selected matter model.
items.strategy: Compute the divergence components directly, then perform the full three-dimensional slice integration and the three-dimensional side-face integration. Both gain exactly the same transverse area A. The negative side-face difference gives the positive slice change through the finite-box theorem. No noncompact limit, physical model, or choice principle is used.

items.title: A prescribed covariant stress-energy tensor need not be conserved
items.statement: In an inertial chart let $\Omega$ be nonempty, open and connected and let $F:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$. The symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T^{ab}=F\eta^{ab}$ is $C^1$, and its continuous force density is $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}=\eta^{ab}\partial_aF=\partial^bF$. It is conserved on $\Omega$ exactly when $F$ is constant; if $F$ is nonconstant then $f$ is not identically zero, although it can vanish at some points. For the smooth explicit witness $\Omega=\mathbb R^4$, $F(x)=(x^1)^2$, one has $f=(0,2x^1,0,0)$, which vanishes on the plane $x^1=0$ and is nonzero off it. The tensor expression $F\eta^{-1}$ is covariant under every affine Lorentz change of inertial chart: for $x'=\Lambda x+a$ the scalar component is $F'(x')=F(\Lambda^{-1}(x'-a))$ and $T'^{ab}=F'\eta^{ab}$. Thus covariance of a prescribed tensor expression does not itself imply conservation; balance is an additional premise. The field is not claimed to be the stress-energy tensor of any of the page's matter models.
items.strategy: Differentiate $F\eta^{ab}$ with the constant inverse metric to obtain the force formula. Nondegeneracy of the metric makes $f=0$ equivalent to all partial derivatives of $F$ vanishing. A $C^1$ scalar is totally differentiable ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]]), so the exact connected-open zero-derivative theorem ([[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]]) gives constancy; the converse follows directly. For $F=(x^1)^2$ compute $f=(0,2x^1,0,0)$, including its stationary plane. Apply the earlier tensor law ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)) with the scalar pulled back to the same physical point and $\Lambda\eta^{-1}\Lambda^{\mathsf T}=\eta^{-1}$. This proves covariance without deriving conservation. No choice principle is used.
